summary: Mont Clare fire tower in Darlington County, SC: an 80-ft wooden tower built about 1940, replaced in 1958 by a 100-ft steel tower; no source says if it still stands.

facts.design: 100-foot steel tower that replaced an 80-foot wooden tower
facts.status_note: The 1958 steel tower is the last structure the sources describe. No source says whether it still stands.

events.note: Side camp constructed a complete forest fire tower unit at Mont Clare; state report year 7/1/40 to 6/30/41
Old wooden tower pulled down; new 100-foot steel structure erected
Ted Bailey named as towerman at Mont Clare, for the past four years
Statewide closure: the commission closed its last forest fire lookout towers

evidence.supports: Mont Clare is in Darlington County
The tower was run by the South Carolina Forestry Commission
A side camp constructed a complete forest fire tower unit at Mont Clare in the 1940-41 report year
evidence.quote: This side camp constructed a complete forest fire tower unit at Mont Clare in Darlington County.

evidence.supports: The state report covers July 1940 to June 1941
evidence.quote: Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/40 to 6/30/1941

evidence.supports: The 80-foot wooden tower was erected by the CCC nearly twenty years before 1958, per the 1958 newspaper
evidence.quote: The 80=foot wooden tower was erected by the now defunct Civilian Conservation Corps, better known as the CCC, nearly twenty years ago.

evidence.supports: The old wooden tower was replaced by a new steel structure in 1957-58
evidence.quote: The old wooden tower located at Mont Clare was replaced by a new steel structure.

evidence.quote: Report of the State Commission of Forestry, 7/1/57 to 6/30/58

evidence.supports: The wooden structure was replaced by a new 100-foot steel tower in May 1958
evidence.quote: The wooden structure was replaced by a new steel 100-foot this month.

OpenStreetMap maps a point named Mont Clare Lookout Tower

sources.title: The South Carolina Forestry Commission (Facebook post on the closing of the last lookout towers)

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1940-41 state report and the 1958 newspaper's 'nearly twenty years' describe the same wooden tower and agree within a year or two. The story uses the state report's year.

notes_for_editor: The 1958 Florence Morning News text is quoted on the eastern lookouts page; the original paper was not read. The replacement and the 100-foot figure rest on that quote and on the state report line for 1957-58. The OSM point is tagged lattice and has a 55 m ele tag, matching the brief. Status after 1958 is not found: no source says whether the steel tower stands, was removed, or was moved, and the OSM point does not establish it. No access, visit or photo facts found. Brief height 30.5 m matches the 100-foot 1958 steel tower. Brief status 'unknown' kept as 'unconfirmed'. Not in the NHLR South Carolina list or the firetower.org former-sites list.
